item.text:
I used your local prior as the baseline and did not re-fetch the structured datasets it already covers. Below is a compact narrative research set for Muhammadu Buhari in Nigeria during 2022, focused on office, authority, constraints, inherited conditions, and the best cross-chapter source families. No scoring.

**Office And Constraints**
Muhammadu Buhari was President and Commander-in-Chief in 2022, in the final year of his second term. The constitutional frame matters: executive power is vested in the president but is subject to the Constitution and laws, and Reuters reporting in June 2022 noted he was constitutionally barred from contesting again. In practice, his room to maneuver was narrowed by term limits, the APC succession process, legislative budget bargaining, courts, and the federal security/economic crises already in motion.

**Retained Sources**

| Source | Publisher / date | Direct URL | Precise fact to carry forward | Period fit / ruler attribution | Limitations / contrary points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Nigeria 1999 Constitution](https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Nigeria_2023) | Constitute Project; current consolidated text | https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Nigeria_2023 | Section 5 vests federal executive power in the president, exercisable directly or through the vice president, ministers, and officers. | Structural authority source for 2022 office and delegated power; clearly attributable to Buhari’s presidency, not to his personal performance. | Legal transcription site, not the official gazette copy; tells you the rule, not how power was actually used. |
| [Buhari Administration at 7: Service to the People, Nothing Else](https://statehouse.gov.ng/buhari-administration-at-7-service-to-the-people-nothing-else/) | State House; 2022-05-28 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/buhari-administration-at-7-service-to-the-people-nothing-else/ | Official self-description that Buhari had served seven years and still had one year left in office. | Strong primary, favorable source for office status and the administration’s own framing in late May 2022. | Self-justifying release; useful for what the presidency claimed, not for independent assessment. |
| [2023 Budget: Budget Of Fiscal Consolidation And Transition](https://statehouse.gov.ng/2023-budget-budget-of-fiscal-consolidation-and-transition/) | State House; 2022-10-07 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/2023-budget-budget-of-fiscal-consolidation-and-transition/ | Buhari said the budget was prepared amid high inflation, low revenues, exchange-rate depreciation, insecurity, and high PMS subsidy costs. | Best primary source for inherited conditions and late-term constraints entering the 2023 transition. | Official framing likely understates policy failures; still valuable because it is Buhari’s own budget speech. |
| [Nigeria: Buhari has no preferred successor, spokesman says](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/6/7/nigerias-buhari-has-no-preferred-successor-spokesman-says) | Al Jazeera, Reuters byline; 2022-06-07 | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/6/7/nigerias-buhari-has-no-preferred-successor-spokesman-says | Buhari was constitutionally barred from contesting and was stepping down after eight years. | Useful for succession constraints and APC intra-party politics in June 2022. | Syndicated Reuters copy on an Al Jazeera page; attribution is secondhand, though still independent. |
| [Nigerian forces hunt for gunmen who killed 50 at church](https://www.clickorlando.com/news/world/2022/06/06/gunmen-at-nigeria-church-shot-from-both-inside-outside/) | Associated Press via ClickOrlando; 2022-06-06 | https://www.clickorlando.com/news/world/2022/06/06/gunmen-at-nigeria-church-shot-from-both-inside-outside/ | Owo church attack killed at least 50 people and used coordinated gunfire/explosives. | High-value security baseline for 2B and 3B; clearly within Buhari’s 2022 security portfolio. | AP syndicated copy; focused on one attack rather than the broader trend line. |
| [Extremists claim responsibility for Nigerian prison attack](https://www.ksat.com/news/world/2022/07/07/extremists-claim-responsibility-for-nigerian-prison-attack/) | Associated Press via KSAT; 2022-07-07 | https://www.ksat.com/news/world/2022/07/07/extremists-claim-responsibility-for-nigerian-prison-attack/ | Kuje prison attack left a mass escape and exposed severe security failure near Abuja. | Strong event source for the security/institutional-capacity chapters. | AP syndicated copy; event-specific, so it needs pairing with broader security sources. |
| [2022 FLOODING: HUMANITARIAN MINISTRY, AGENCIES MEET TO MITIGATE AND REDUCE IMPACT](https://fmhds.gov.ng/news/2022-flooding-humanitarian-ministry-agencies-meet-to-mitigate-and-reduce-impact/) | Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs; 2022-10-11 | https://fmhds.gov.ng/news/2022-flooding-humanitarian-ministry-agencies-meet-to-mitigate-and-reduce-impact/ | Official figures: over 1.4 million displaced, about 500 dead, and extensive farm/home damage. | Primary evidence for inherited disaster burden, food insecurity, and state response limits in 2022. | Official count, likely revised over time; does not itself assign blame or explain causation. |
| [Buhari seeks approval of N4trn for petrol subsidy in 2022](https://www.thecable.ng/buhari-seeks-approval-of-n4trn-for-petrol-subsidy-in-2022/) | TheCable; 2022-04-07 | https://www.thecable.ng/buhari-seeks-approval-of-n4trn-for-petrol-subsidy-in-2022/ | Buhari asked the legislature for N4 trillion for petrol subsidy, citing Russian-Ukraine war and domestic production shortfalls. | Useful domestic press source for the subsidy/fiscal strain chapter cluster. | Local independent outlet, but still reporting on a budget request rather than final fiscal outcomes. |
| [ASUU finally suspends eight-month-old strike](https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-asuu-suspends-strike-after-eight-months/) | TheCable; 2022-10-14 | https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-asuu-suspends-strike-after-eight-months/ | University lecturers had been on strike since February 14, 2022; the dispute crippled higher education for most of the year. | Good for 6B and 8B because it shows education-system stress and government bargaining limits. | Mostly labor/education angle; does not by itself prove broader governance quality. |
| [Nigeria Development Update: Nigeria’s Choice](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099305012142215802) | World Bank; document date 2022-11-30, disclosure 2022-12-15 | https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099305012142215802 | Nigeria faced deteriorating macro conditions, slowing growth, and the need to restore macro stability, competitiveness, and social protection. | Best multilateral macro source for 5B, 6B, 7B, and 8B context. | Technocratic and country-level, not ruler-specific; strong on structure, weak on attribution. |
| [Nigeria: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Nigeria](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/02/16/nigeria-2022-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-the-529842) | IMF; 2023-02-16 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/02/16/nigeria-2022-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-the-529842 | Inflation was elevated, fuel subsidies remained a major fiscal drain, and stronger revenue mobilization and exchange-rate reform were needed. | Strong for inherited economic conditions and late-2022 policy constraints. | Macro and institutional, not ruler-specific; useful as an outside check on official claims. |
| [World Report 2023: Nigeria](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/nigeria) | Human Rights Watch; covers events of 2022 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/nigeria | Details insecurity, abuses by security forces, press/expression issues, and poverty in 2022. | Best critical human-rights family for 2B, 3B, and 4B. | Advocacy lens; strong on abuses and rights patterns, less useful for formal institutional detail. |

**Compact Event Map**

| Date / period | Event | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Jan-Feb 2022 | ASUU strike, fuel scarcity, subsidy pressure | Shows inherited governance strain, education disruption, and cost-of-living pressure. |
| Mar 29, 2022 | Abuja-Kaduna train attack | Demonstrates persistent insecurity and the state’s inability to secure key transport routes. |
| Apr 7, 2022 | Buhari requests N4 trillion for petrol subsidy | Signals fiscal stress, policy lock-in, and weak macro room to maneuver. |
| Jun 5-7, 2022 | Owo church attack | A major civilian massacre that anchors the 2022 security picture. |
| Jun 2022 | APC succession fight and no preferred successor messaging | Shows political constraint from the approaching transition and party machinery. |
| Jul 6, 2022 | Kuje prison attack | Exposes security failure near Abuja and weakness in custodial protection. |
| Oct 2022 | Catastrophic floods | Severe inherited disaster burden, food-security damage, and emergency-response strain. |
| Oct 2022 | ASUU strike ends after eight months | Confirms the depth of the education crisis and bargaining limits. |
| Nov-Dec 2022 | IMF and World Bank issue deteriorating macro warnings | Reinforces the inherited economic fragility and subsidy/inflation problem. |

**Chapter Source Plan**

| Chapter | Best retained sources | What they cover |
|---|---|---|
| 1B | Constitution; State House 7-year release; Reuters/Al Jazeera successor story | Office, authority, term limit, succession constraint. |
| 2B | AP Owo; AP Kuje; NEMA floods | Conflict exposure, civilian harm, state security failures, disaster burden. |
| 3B | HRW World Report 2023; AP Owo; AP Kuje | Rights abuses, killings, insecurity, and accountability gaps. |
| 4B | Constitution; State House 7-year; Reuters/Al Jazeera successor story; HRW | Political freedom, institutional limits, election-period constraints, civic space. |
| 5B | World Bank NDU; IMF Article IV; TheCable subsidy request | GDP, inflation, subsidy drain, exchange-rate pressure, fiscal weakness. |
| 6B | NEMA floods; ASUU strike; World Bank NDU | Human development stress, education disruption, welfare shock, disaster effects. |
| 7B | IMF Article IV; World Bank NDU; State House 2023 budget speech | Corruption/governance context, fiscal drain, reform need, institutional weakness. |
| 8B | State House 2023 budget speech; IMF Article IV; World Bank NDU; HRW | Government effectiveness, implementation constraints, and the gap between stated goals and delivery. |
